title: Yeh'kinya, the Ancient Egg, and Hakkar
summary: Spirits, tablets and an ancient vessel draw a stranger into Yeh’kinya’s concealed purpose. A victory in the Sunken Temple gives way to a warning and an appeal for aid.
opening: From a desert port, the search reaches forests, high ruins and the drowned halls of the Sunken Temple. An egg receives an essence, and the fuller prophecy reveals the purpose hidden beneath Yeh’kinya’s promise.

chapters.title: The request and the relics
chapters.body:
At Steamwheedle Port, Yeh’kinya asked a stranger to capture the spirits of Vale Screechers. He supplied a bramble, but his first words did not disclose the full purpose of the gathering. Beyond the desert harbor waited Feralas’s forested hills. A small request opened the search toward a power whose name had yet to reveal its danger.

From harbor dust, the seeker entered Feralas’s green shade and gathered the Vale Screechers’ spirits with the bramble. Their essence returned toward Yeh’kinya. The work had yielded what he sought without making his purpose plain. Within the forest’s living creatures, the stranger had found the beginning of a design that would reach far beyond the hills.

Back in Tanaris, Yeh’kinya spoke of Hakkar and the prophecy of Mosh’aru. He asked for its tablets. In his telling, the gathered spirits belonged to a greater purpose, though the seeker had not yet learned all that he meant to do. The search turned toward written words that might explain the essence already placed in his keeping.

Within Zul’Farrak’s sandstone halls, guardians held two tablets of Mosh’aru. The recovered prophecy described a means of containing an essence. The search had found the words Yeh’kinya wanted, but his whole purpose remained concealed. From the desert ruins, the tablets returned toward a plan whose promised safety could not yet be trusted.

At Jintha’Alor, the Ancient Egg waited in a cave behind the high amphitheater. The seeker recovered it and returned toward Yeh’kinya with the vessel his plan required. Tablets and relic had come from distant places into one keeping. Their gathering brought the stranger nearer the rite he had described, while the full burden of that trust remained unknown.

At the port, Yeh’kinya received the egg and the tablets. His next direction led to the Sunken Temple, where a rite would call forth Hakkar’s essence. From forest spirits and desert writings, the search had reached a drowned sanctuary. What had been gathered into his plan would now be used, and the stranger’s trust approached the danger hidden within it.

chapters.title: The avatar and the egg
chapters.body:
Deep in the drowned temple, the seeker reached the Sanctum of the Fallen God. Atal’ai bloodrinkers stood among its threats. The tablets and Ancient Egg had brought Yeh’kinya’s design into the old halls. Beneath the temple’s dark waters, the rite began, drawing the scattered preparations toward the presence they had been meant to summon.

An avatar of Hakkar appeared, a skeletal wind serpent called into the Sunken Temple. The seeker fought and defeated that summoned presence. Hakkar’s later physical manifestation still lay beyond this encounter. Within the drowned sanctuary, the victory had reached an avatar and the essence the rite sought, leaving the greater danger outside the limits of the battle.

The avatar’s essence was placed within the Ancient Egg. Yeh’kinya promised to keep the vessel safe. Yet the egg stirred. The rite had reached its intended end without offering certainty that the danger was contained. Back at the desert port, the object carried a troubling life within it, and the seeker’s trust had begun to meet an unanswered warning.

chapters.title: Six tablets and a revelation
chapters.body:
Prospector Ironboot sent the seeker after the remaining tablets of Mosh’aru. Beyond the first pair, other words survived that could change the meaning of Yeh’kinya’s plan. The search opened again. What had seemed a completed rite now depended upon a fuller reading of the prophecy, and upon knowledge its keeper had not placed before the stranger.

In the Eastern Plaguelands, the search climbed to an old troll ziggurat. Two more tablets were recovered among its stones and carried back toward Ironboot. The prophecy’s scattered words had survived within another wounded country. Their recovery brought the inquiry nearer the meaning of the egg that had begun to stir in Yeh’kinya’s keeping.

The final pair lay among the Smolderthorn trolls in Blackrock Spire. With their recovery, the six tablets could be read together. Ironboot would weigh what the fuller prophecy meant for the Ancient Egg. The search had crossed ruined places to gather words withheld from its first beginning; now those words could challenge the purpose Yeh’kinya had claimed.

Ironboot read a warning in the tablets: the egg might serve Hakkar’s rebirth within Zul’Gurub. The seeker had not witnessed that return, but the prospect changed the meaning of the temple rite. The avatar’s defeat could have supplied a later danger rather than ended it. Yeh’kinya’s promise of safe keeping now stood beneath a suspicion the stranger could no longer leave unanswered.

Confronted with the fuller prophecy, Yeh’kinya revealed that he intended to use the egg in Hakkar’s return. The promised containment had hidden another purpose. Tales of his escape spoke of a green wind serpent, but the disclosure itself was plain: the seeker had helped gather what he needed. The threatened rebirth remained beyond that confrontation, and aid against it had still to be sought.

On Yojamba Isle, the seeker was directed to Molthor and asked to bring aid against Hakkar. The egg’s gathering had ended in the revelation of a danger it was meant to serve. Beyond the island waited Zul’Gurub and another campaign. Here the journey closed upon an appeal, carrying the warning onward without yet answering what the coming struggle would cost.

reviewNote: Complete illustrated research transcript with 15 nodes, eight Classic-area environments, original actor/group/relic art, relational scene states, and per-beat source/citation/claim records. Lore review remains open: secondary Classic quest locators, original-client dialogue/build verification, in-game resemblance comparison, art composition and voice audition. The Sunken Temple summons an avatar; the Burning Crusade manual separates it from Zul'Gurub's later physical summoning. Yeh'kinya's motives and escape are attributed. The story ends at the Yojamba request for aid and does not show the raid.
